facts.statement: Lirainosaurus is a genus of titanosaur sauropod named for its slender appearance, meaning "slender lizard" in Basque and Greek.
facts.quote: Lirainosaurus (meaning "slender lizard"; from the Basque lirain, meaning "slender", and the Greek sauros, meaning "lizard") is a genus of titanosaur sauropod which lived in what is now Spain.

facts.statement: Lirainosaurus was a relatively small sauropod, measuring 4 to 6 meters long and weighing 2 to 4 metric tons.
facts.quote: It was a relatively small sauropod, measuring 4 m long, possibly up to 6 m long for the largest individuals, and weighed about 2 - 4 MT.

facts.statement: The type species Lirainosaurus astibiae was described by Sanz and colleagues in 1999.
facts.quote: The type species, Lirainosaurus astibiae, was described by Sanz, Powell, Le Loeuff, Martinez, and Pereda-Suberbiola in 1999.

facts.statement: The genus was originally defined based on a skull fragment, teeth, vertebrae, and limb bones found in Laño, northern Spain.
facts.quote: This genus was based on a skull fragment, isolated teeth, several vertebrae including the holotype - an anterior caudal vertebra, and appendicular bones from the Late Cretaceous of Laño (northern Spain).

facts.statement: By 2015, researchers reported that 150 bones had been recovered from Lirainosaurus sites.
facts.quote: En 2015 se informó que el número de huesos recuperados era de 150.

facts.statement: In 2015, researchers concluded that fossils found in Chera, Valencia, were not definitively Lirainosaurus.
facts.quote: En 2015 se concluyó que no había evidencia de que se tratara de Lirainosaurus.

facts.statement: Only two fragmentary osteoderms have been found, suggesting Lirainosaurus had less extensive armor than titanosaurians like Ampelosaurus.
facts.quote: Hasta la fecha, solo se han encontrado dos osteodermos fragmentarios , lo que puede sugerir que la armadura de Lirainosaurusno era tan extensa como la de los titanosaurios como Ampelosaurus.

facts.statement: Lirainosaurus possessed teeth shaped like pins.
facts.quote: Los dientes de Lirainosaurus tienen forma de alfiler.

facts.statement: Lirainosaurus lived between the Late Campanian and Early Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Marine biostratigraphic testing of the formation places its age somewhere between Late Campanian to Early Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: Lirainosaurus shared its environment with Ampelosaurus, Rhabdodon, ankylosaurs, and dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: Other contemporary dinosaurs in the Bellevue layer include the titanosaur sauropod Ampelosaurus, the rhabdodontid Rhabdodon and indeterminate ankylosaur and Dromaeosauridae elements.

facts.statement: A 2016 study suggested Lirainosaurus was phylogenetically closer to Alamosaurus and Opisthocoelicaudia than to Saltasaurus.
facts.quote: The results of an unpublished SVPCA abstract published in 2016 narrow down the exact position of Lirainosaurus by placing it as closer to Alamosaurus and Opisthocoelicaudia than to Saltasaurus.

facts.statement: In 2018, Diez Diaz and colleagues created the subfamily Lirainosaurinae to include Lirainosaurus, Ampelosaurus, and Atsinganosaurus.
facts.quote: Later, Diez Diaz et al. (2018) erected Lirainosaurinae to accommodate Lirainosaurus as well as Ampelosaurus and Atsinganosaurus.

facts.statement: Diez Díaz et al. established the subfamily Lirainosaurinae in 2018 to group Lirainosaurus with Ampelosaurus and Atsinganosaurus.
facts.quote: Más tarde, Diez Díaz et al. en 2018 erigieron Lirainosaurinae para acomodar a Lirainosaurus , así como a Ampelosaurus y Atsinganosaurus.

facts.statement: Due to extensive descriptions of its fossils, Lirainosaurus was the most studied titanosaur in Europe in 2015.
facts.quote: Debido a todas las descripciones, Lirainosaurus fue el titanosaurio más estudiado en Europa en 2015.

facts.statement: Fossils of Lirainosaurus have been found at the Bellevue site in the northern Pyrenees.
facts.quote: Se han encontrado muestras en el sitio de Bellevue, en el norte de los Pirineos

facts.statement: Marine biostratigraphic tests place the age of the formation containing Lirainosaurus fossils between the late Campanian and early Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Las pruebas bioestratagráficas marinas de la formación ubican su edad en algún lugar entre el Campaniano tardío y el Maastrichtiano temprano

facts.statement: Contemporaneous dinosaurs at the Bellevue site included the titanosaur Ampelosaurus, the hadrosaur Rhabdodon, and indeterminate ankylosaurian and dromaeosaurid elements.
facts.quote: Otros dinosaurios contemporáneos en la capa de Bellevue incluyen el saurópodo titanosaurio Ampelosaurus, el rabdodonto Rhabdodon y elementos indeterminados de anquilosauriano y Dromaeosauridae

facts.statement: Local stratigraphy at the Fox-Amphoux-Métisson site shows the same facies succession as the Aix-en-Provence basin, dating to the late Campanian to early Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la estratigrafía local presenta la misma sucesión de facies que en la cuenca de Aix-en-Provence, que también se encuentra en la era de Campaniano tardía a Maastrichtiense temprana

facts.statement: Lirainosaurus belongs to the parent group Lirainosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Lirainosaurinae

facts.statement: Lirainosaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Lirainosaurus lived from 83.6 to 66 million years ago during the Campanian to Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 10 recorded fossil occurrences of Lirainosaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 10

rejected.statement: Lirainosaurus was only slightly heavier than dwarf sauropods like Europasaurus.
rejected.quote: Lirainosaurus era solo un poco más pesado que los saurópodos enanos como el Europasaurus.
